22. The law regard burden of proof is envisaged in section 101 of the Evidence Act that the burden of proof lies on the party ` who substantially asserts the affirmative of the issue and not upon the party who denies it. The party on whom the onus of proof lies must, in order to succeed establish a prima facie case. He cannot, on failure to do take advantage of the weakness of his adversary's case. He must succeed by the strength of his own right. In a criminal trial, the burden of proving the guilt of the accused beyond all reasonable doubts always, rests on the prosecution and on its failure, it cannot fall back upon the evidence adduced by the accused in support of his defence to rest its case solely thereon. In criminal case it is for the prosecution to bring guilt home to the accused. The fundamental and basic presumption in the administration of criminal law and justice delivery system is the innocence of the alleged accused and till 

 33. In the instant case, the learned trial court basing on presumption having no basis convicted the accused under section 302 of the Penal Code and sentenced him to imprisonment for life. The primary question for consideration in a murder case is whether the prosecution has been able to prove conclusively that, the husband alone killed his wife. On reappraisal and scrutiny of evidence we find no such evidence that the appellant husband killed his wife and thus it is be improper to substitute moral conviction for legal evidence. It is not found that the victim lying dead in the room of her husband rather it has been proved that the victim died on the road. Such evidence has clearly caste a serious doubt as to the guilt of the appellant. These evidence, gave suspicion as to the guilt of the appellant and in the absence of reliable evidence it is not sufficient to convict the appellant. In murder change-against husband for killing his wife in his house, generally no eye witness is found. In such circumstances, court is to depend on circumstantial evidence. But in the instant case, there is no such circumstantial evidence which binds the accused for convicting under section 302 of the penal Code. In 'the absence of incriminating conduct and circumstances the sentence under this section does not lie. Killing of a woman is certainly inhuman no doubt. But one can not be convicted on presumption, conjecture and surmise. It is not proper to presume that the victim might have been killed in the house of the accused without any legal evidence. It is improper to substitute moral conviction for legal evidence.
